name: Claims Lodgement Officer formats numbers as digits after switching to WhatsApp mid-claim

chat_history.message: Hi, I started lodging this on a call earlier but got disconnected, so I'm picking it back up here on WhatsApp. It's a property claim, policy POL-204958.
There was a break-in at 207 Example Street, Perth on the 3rd of March around 9pm. You can reach me on 0433 221 190, name Daniel Ross.
Can you read back the address you've got for me, just to double check?

success_condition: This is a text-only WhatsApp conversation (system__is_text_only is true) where the claimant says they are continuing a claim they started on a phone call, then asks the agent to read back the property address. Per the channel-specific number formatting rule, on text-only conversations ALL numbers must be written as digits, not spelled out as words — this applies to every number, not only phone/policy/registration numbers, which is a broader rule than writing numbers as words for voice. The agent's response must state the street number as a digit (e.g. '207'), not as words (e.g. 'two hundred and seven' or 'two-oh-seven'). The response must also contain no markdown formatting symbols (no asterisks, no bullet characters, no headers) — plain prose only, not a line-per-field layout.

success_examples.response: Yep, I've got 207 Example Street, Perth for you — is that right?
Sure — that's 207 Example Street, Perth, contact 0433 221 190 for Daniel Ross. Let me know if anything needs fixing.

failure_examples.response: Sure, I have two hundred and seven Example Street, Perth on file.
Sure — that's two-oh-seven Example Street, Perth, is that correct?

Here's what I have:
*Address:* 207 Example Street, Perth
*Contact:* 0433 221 190
